clue.text: Write smash hit composition featuring No1 from Crosby

definitions.text: Write smash hit composition featuring No1 from Crosby

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the preceding words are arranged afresh
number one from a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the name is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, thirteen letters of fodder
the opening letter of the singer's surname

explanation.surface: A songwriter is urged to pen a hit with Bing Crosby leading the vocals.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: WHITE CHRISTMAS is the composition that became Crosby's biggest smash hit, and it is spelt from the shuffled words plus his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin's song, sung by Bing Crosby, is the best-selling single of all time, a genuine smash.

clue.text: Gloss over Earl upsetting lover

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits over the next, so the Earl's letter comes on top
upsetting tips something upside down, which in a down entry means the word for lover reads bottom to top

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for Earl
leman is an archaic word for a sweetheart or paramour

explanation.surface: Someone smooths over a scandal in which an aristocrat has spurned his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloss over' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'Gloss' alone is the definition, a noun. LEMAN is an old word for a lover that crosswords use often.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a hard shiny paint or coating, and a gloss is likewise a shiny finish applied to surfaces.

clue.text: Page One in today’s fresh hellscape

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made new, so the word before it is remade in a new order
in places the page and the one inside the reworked word

blocks.note: p is the usual abbreviation for page
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A newspaper's front page reports another fresh nightmare in today's world.
explanation.definitionFit: A dystopia is an imagined society of misery and oppression, so a nightmarish world is a fair synonym.

clue.text: That woman’s acquired the first car lease in the county

indicators.note: something acquired is taken in, so the woman's word holds the car inside it

blocks.note: the possessive pronoun for that woman
the Model T Ford was the first mass-produced car
to lease something is to hire it

explanation.surface: A woman has picked up a vintage car on a leasing deal somewhere in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T Ford, launched in 1908, is often called the first car for ordinary people, hence 'the first car'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hertfordshire is one of the home counties of England, bordering Greater London to the north.

clue.text: A piece of cake that might be served on a blanket?

definitions.text: that might be served on a blanket

blocks.note: first meaning: something very easy

blocks.clueFragment: that might be served on a blanket
blocks.note: second meaning: an outdoor meal laid out on a rug on the grass

explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' looks like food to be served, which suits the blanket; in fact it is the idiom for an easy task.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally an easy task is called a picnic, and literally the word names an open-air meal eaten from a rug.

clue.text: Sid and Gene organised debut for Rudolph Valentino, for one

indicators.note: organised means arranged into order, so the two names are rearranged
a debut is a first appearance, so only the opening letter of the name is used

blocks.note: the two names taken as written, without the 'and'
the first letter of the first name

explanation.surface: Two promoters arrange the screen debut of the silent-film heartthrob Rudolph Valentino.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs Valentino with Rudolph, the silent-film star, but the definition means Valentino Garavani, the Italian fashion house founder.
explanation.definitionFit: Valentino Garavani is a celebrated Italian fashion couturier, an example of someone who creates clothes.

clue.text: Polish tree bearing first of durian fruit

indicators.note: a tree bearing something carries it, so the tree word holds a letter within it
first of points to the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: to hone is to sharpen or polish
the yew is an evergreen tree
the opening letter of durian

explanation.surface: A Polish tree is described as bearing the pungent tropical durian fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised 'Polish' suggests the nationality; it is the verb meaning to smooth or sharpen.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeydew is a variety of melon with pale sweet flesh, so it is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Master of suspense fondly embracing European design style

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so the director's nickname wraps around the European letter

blocks.note: Alfred Hitchcock, the master of suspense, was fondly known as Hitch
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Hitchcock affectionately hugs a European in a scene about design.
explanation.definitionFit: High-tech is an architectural and interior style that shows off industrial materials and exposed structure.

clue.text: Holding up traffic?

blocks.note: surface reading: causing a jam that stops vehicles on the road
setter's reading: robbing travellers at gunpoint on the open road, as old mounted bandits did

explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding up' sounds like delaying cars; it is the stick-up sense, aimed at those travelling the king's roads.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the crime of a mounted bandit stopping coaches on the road to rob passengers, also used for overcharging.

clue.text: Wave breaking over vessel that might cause nausea

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting over another comes before it

blocks.note: a roller is a long wave that curls and breaks on the shore
a coaster is a ship trading along the coast

explanation.surface: A wave crashes over a small ship, enough to make anyone seasick.
explanation.walkthrough: The seasickness picture leads to boats, but the definition is a fairground ride known for turning stomachs.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground ride with steep drops and loops often leaves passengers dizzy and queasy, so it might make someone sick.

clue.text: Attract casual worker close to bankrupt

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: a temp is a temporary member of staff
the final letter of bankrupt

explanation.surface: A firm on the verge of bankruptcy tries to attract a casual worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to entice or lure them, much as to attract draws someone towards something.

clue.text: Licking Manx cat in 4 town?

indicators.note: the Manx breed has no tail, so the animal word loses its last letter
in puts the shortened animal inside the name of the town

blocks.note: Tring is a market town in the answer to 4, Hertfordshire
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A tailless Isle of Man cat gives itself a lick somewhere in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Licking' suggests a cat grooming itself, but it means a heavy defeat. A Manx cat is a tailless breed from the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A licking is a sound beating, and a trouncing is likewise a decisive defeat in a contest.

clue.text: Charlie plays remixed intro to Oasis song

indicators.note: a remix is a reworked version of a track, so the word before it is rearranged
the intro of something is its start, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written
the first letter of the band name

explanation.surface: A DJ called Charlie spins a remix built on an Oasis intro.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a Caribbean musical style from Trinidad, and a calypso is a single tune in that style.

clue.text: City fortune secured from the East

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means reading right to left

blocks.note: fortune in the sense of chance
to secure a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: Someone made their fortune trading goods from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the East' sounds like a trading route; it tells you to read the word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucknow is a large historic city in northern India, capital of the state of Uttar Pradesh.

clue.text: Opening of really sad story Macron broadcast somewhere up north

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the words are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of really
taken as written, fourteen letters of fodder

explanation.surface: The French president goes on air to tell a genuinely gloomy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: ROSS AND CROMARTY is a historic county in the far north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Scottish county lies in the Highlands, far to the north of Britain, so it is a place up north.

clue.text: Crumbling old Paris side lane

indicators.note: something crumbling falls to pieces, so the words break apart and reform

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crumbling lane down a back street of old Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: A SLIP ROAD is the British name for a motorway on-ramp or off-ramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A short road joining or leaving a motorway runs alongside the main carriageway, a fair description of a lane at the side.

clue.text: Important woman from Omaha ran independently

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters inside these words
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A prominent woman from Nebraska stood for office as an independent.
explanation.walkthrough: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska, USA; 'independently' gives only I, a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharani is the wife of a maharaja or a female ruler in India, certainly a woman of high rank.

clue.text: Leaves second leg, long drained of energy

indicators.note: drained of something means emptied of it, so the energy letter is removed

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
pins is slang for legs
to long for something is to ache for it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A runner leaves for the second leg, long since drained of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb about departing; it is the plural noun for foliage eaten as vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a plant grown for its dark green edible foliage, so it is a crop of leaves.

clue.text: Article on current mass American hostility

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it, so the article comes first

blocks.note: the indefinite article
I is the symbol for electric current
m is the symbol for mass
US is short for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A newspaper article on current events stirs widespread American hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus means ill will or animosity felt towards someone, so it is a close synonym of antagonism.

clue.text: Tragedy beginning to overtake Time magazine

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of overtake
t is the abbreviation for time
Hello! is a British celebrity magazine

explanation.surface: A tragic story starts to take over the cover of Time magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time magazine' reads as one title, but it splits into T and a different magazine, HELLO!, a British celebrity weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's play about the Moor of Venice, one of his great tragedies.

clue.text: Ladies and gents wear periodically made less figure-hugging

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the ladies and the gents are both public toilets, informally loos
the second and fourth letters of wear

explanation.surface: Men and women are told to wear their clothes baggier from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the Ladies' and 'the Gents' are the names for women's and men's public toilets, so together they are LOOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that is looser hangs away from the body rather than clinging tightly to the wearer's shape.

clue.text: Mum runs lodgings accommodating artist festival

indicators.note: lodgings accommodating someone house them, so the artist goes inside

blocks.note: an informal word for mother
r is the cricket abbreviation for runs
digs is British slang for rented rooms
RA stands for Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A mother runs a boarding house that puts up a painter during carnival.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras, or Shrove Tuesday, is celebrated with carnivals and parades, notably in New Orleans.

clue.text: Figure in polyester homburg

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A figure is pictured wearing a hat made of synthetic fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: A homburg is a felt hat with a dented crown, which helps the picture of a well-dressed figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb, or rhombus, is a geometrical shape with four equal sides, so a plane figure.

clue.text: Small gallery showcasing university artwork

indicators.note: a gallery showcasing something displays it within its walls, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for small
the Tate is the famous London art gallery
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A modest gallery mounts an exhibition of student artwork from the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast sculpture of a figure, an example of a piece of visual art.

clue.text: Cupid maybe was king here, it’s said

indicators.note: it's said tells us to go by how the words sound when spoken

blocks.note: to have been king is to have reigned, and here dropped of its h becomes 'ere

explanation.surface: Visitors are told that the god of love once ruled on this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cupid' suggests the Roman god of love; here he is one of Santa's sleigh-pullers, named in the poem 'A Visit from St Nicholas'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid is one of Santa Claus's team of flying sleigh animals, so he is an example of the antlered deer.
